# PHPRegex

> Static analysis, linter & logic solver for PHP regular expressions. PHPRegex parses PCRE-style regexes into an immutable AST and answers questions about them: validity ruled as PHP's own engine would rule it, ReDoS safety with a proof or a witness, lint findings with fixes, provably equivalent rewrites, sample strings a pattern matches, and pattern-to-pattern logic (equivalence, intersection, subset) via automata.

Install: composer require --dev php-regex/regex-cli:2.x-dev for the CLI, or choose a focused php-regex/* package for parser, toolkit, static-analysis, editor, and framework integrations
Docs: https://php-regex.com/docs/
Repository: https://github.com/php-regex/php-regex
License: MIT

## Learn

- [Playground](https://php-regex.com/): a pattern and a subject run on the real PHP and PCRE2 in the browser, in the PHP version you pick, with the explanation, the lint findings and the tree
- [Documentation](https://php-regex.com/docs/): the documentation map, organized by task
- [Quick Start](https://php-regex.com/quick-start/): install and first analysis in a few runnable steps
- [Regex 101 tutorial](https://php-regex.com/tutorial/): regular expressions from basics to real-world PHP, ten chapters
- [Regex in PHP](https://php-regex.com/guides/regex-in-php/): how PCRE behaves inside preg_* — delimiters, flags, the functions and their return values
- [PHP regex modifiers](https://php-regex.com/guides/php-regex-modifiers/): every modifier of PHP, what each one changes, and the flags of other languages it answers
- [preg_replace](https://php-regex.com/guides/preg-replace/): every match or the first, references, arrays and callbacks
- [PHP regex cheat sheet](https://php-regex.com/cheat-sheet/): every symbol on one line with a checked example, the preg functions, and the fix of each message PHP prints

## Integrations

- [Guides index](https://php-regex.com/guides/): every integration on one page, with its install command
- [PHPStan](https://php-regex.com/guides/phpstan/): regex findings inside static analysis
- [Psalm](https://php-regex.com/guides/psalm/): $matches typed from the pattern
- [Rector](https://php-regex.com/guides/rector/): preg_* calls rewritten to the string functions they provably equal
- [PHPUnit](https://php-regex.com/guides/phpunit/): match, compilation and proven-linearity assertions for your test suite
- [Infection](https://php-regex.com/guides/infection/): mutators for the regex literals of preg_* calls, each mutant with the subject that kills it
- [Laravel](https://php-regex.com/guides/laravel/): Regex service, facade, artisan commands
- [Symfony](https://php-regex.com/guides/symfony/): bundle, service, console commands
- [LSP](https://php-regex.com/guides/lsp/): diagnostics, hovers and code actions in any editor
- [MCP](https://php-regex.com/guides/mcp/): validation, explanations, layout, translation and ReDoS verdicts for a coding agent, over the Model Context Protocol
- [CLI](https://php-regex.com/guides/cli/): seventeen subcommands, config files, output formats, CI recipes
- [ReDoS guide](https://php-regex.com/guides/redos/): verdicts, guarantees, confirmed mode, fixes
- [Formatting patterns](https://php-regex.com/guides/formatting/): a long pattern laid out over lines, or compacted to one, without changing what it matches
- [Cookbook](https://php-regex.com/cookbook/): ready-made patterns with their safety verdicts
  - [Email](https://php-regex.com/cookbook/email/): a simplified RFC 5322 address — what it accepts, what it refuses, why it is linear
  - [URL](https://php-regex.com/cookbook/url/): http and https URLs — what it accepts, what it refuses, why it is linear
  - [UUID](https://php-regex.com/cookbook/uuid/): versions 1 to 5, with what it accepts and refuses
  - [IPv4](https://php-regex.com/cookbook/ipv4/): four octets from 0 to 255, without a leading zero
  - [IPv6](https://php-regex.com/cookbook/ipv6/): the full form, eight groups of hex digits, and filter_var() for the rest
  - [Date](https://php-regex.com/cookbook/date/): ISO 8601, US and European formats, and checkdate() to complete them
  - [Time](https://php-regex.com/cookbook/time/): 24-hour with or without seconds, and 12-hour with AM or PM
  - [Date-time](https://php-regex.com/cookbook/datetime/): a date, a T, a time and an optional zone offset, in ISO 8601
  - [Slug](https://php-regex.com/cookbook/slug/): lower-case letters and digits in segments separated by single hyphens
  - [Username](https://php-regex.com/cookbook/username/): 3 to 32 characters from a letter, with the patterns of Linux, GitHub and X for comparison
  - [Password](https://php-regex.com/cookbook/password/): eight characters with a lower-case letter, a capital and a digit, or twelve with a symbol too
  - [Phone number](https://php-regex.com/cookbook/phone-number/): E.164 and North American formats, digits only
  - [Credit card](https://php-regex.com/cookbook/credit-card/): 13 to 19 digits, and Visa, Mastercard, Amex and Discover by their first digits
  - [Hex color](https://php-regex.com/cookbook/hex-color/): #rgb and #rrggbb
  - [Semantic version](https://php-regex.com/cookbook/semantic-version/): the regular expression SemVer suggests, and why it is linear
- [Troubleshooting](https://php-regex.com/troubleshooting/): common errors and their fixes

## Concepts

- [Key concepts](https://php-regex.com/concepts/): the fundamental ideas behind PHPRegex, explained for beginners
- [What is an AST?](https://php-regex.com/concepts/ast/): the structured representation of a pattern every analysis walks
- [Understanding Visitors](https://php-regex.com/concepts/visitors/): how operations run over the tree without changing it
- [ReDoS Deep Dive](https://php-regex.com/concepts/redos/): why patterns backtrack catastrophically and what is provable
- [PCRE vs Other Engines](https://php-regex.com/concepts/pcre/): where PHP's engine sits among the others

## Reference

- [Reference index](https://php-regex.com/reference/): the reference material on one page
- [Lint rules](https://php-regex.com/reference/rules/): every diagnostic, rule and optimization
- [API](https://php-regex.com/reference/api/): entry points, return objects, exceptions
- [Diagnostics](https://php-regex.com/reference/diagnostics/): error types, messages, and how to map them to fixes
- [Errors PHP prints](https://php-regex.com/reference/diagnostics/#the-errors-php-prints): one page per warning preg_* prints and per error of a match — the pattern that prints it, the cause, the fix, the code PHPRegex gives
- [Unknown modifier](https://php-regex.com/reference/diagnostics/unknown-modifier/): a delimiter inside the pattern, or a modifier PHP does not know
- [No ending delimiter found](https://php-regex.com/reference/diagnostics/no-ending-delimiter/): a delimiter missing, or escaped by the backslash before it
- [Missing terminating ] for character class](https://php-regex.com/reference/diagnostics/missing-terminating-bracket-for-character-class/): a [ that no ] closes
- [Missing closing parenthesis](https://php-regex.com/reference/diagnostics/missing-closing-parenthesis/): a group that never closes
- [Reference to non-existent subpattern](https://php-regex.com/reference/diagnostics/reference-to-non-existent-subpattern/): a backreference or a call that names no group
- [Lookbehind assertion is not fixed length](https://php-regex.com/reference/diagnostics/lookbehind-assertion-is-not-fixed-length/): a lookbehind with no bounded length, and the rewrites
- [Backtrack limit exhausted](https://php-regex.com/reference/diagnostics/backtrack-limit-exhausted/): preg_match() returned false: the loop and the fixes
- [Malformed UTF-8 characters](https://php-regex.com/reference/diagnostics/malformed-utf-8-characters/): the subject of a /u pattern that is not UTF-8
- [PCRE2 does not support \u](https://php-regex.com/reference/diagnostics/pcre2-does-not-support-unicode-escapes/): the \uXXXX of other languages, and \x{...} instead
- [Allocation of JIT memory failed](https://php-regex.com/reference/diagnostics/allocation-of-jit-memory-failed/): PHP turns its JIT off and matches on: executable memory denied, or pcre.jit=0
- [JIT compilation failed](https://php-regex.com/reference/diagnostics/jit-compilation-failed/): thousands of capturing groups, the wordings by release, pcre.jit=0
- [Diagnostics cheat sheet](https://php-regex.com/reference/diagnostics-cheatsheet/): the quick fix of each common error, each linked to its page
- [JSON output](https://php-regex.com/reference/json-output/): every key the regex command and the Symfony and Laravel reports print
- [Feature support matrix](https://php-regex.com/reference/feature-support-matrix/): which PCRE construct each analysis layer supports
- [Correctness contracts](https://php-regex.com/reference/correctness-contracts/): what is sound, what is heuristic, per feature
- [Backward compatibility](https://php-regex.com/reference/backward-compatibility/): what each release may change
- [Extraction coverage](https://php-regex.com/reference/extraction-coverage/): which calls the lint, the language server and the static analysers read a pattern from
- [Capture shapes](https://php-regex.com/reference/capture-shapes/): what preg_match() writes into $matches
- [Pattern info](https://php-regex.com/reference/pattern-info/): the facts PCRE2 computes on every compiled pattern
- [Prefilters](https://php-regex.com/reference/prefilters/): when a string function can answer before preg_match()
- [PCRE2 conformance](https://php-regex.com/reference/pcre2-conformance/): measured against PHP's engine on the official test suite
- [Sonar](https://php-regex.com/reference/sonar/): where each SonarPHP regex rule maps to a PHPRegex identifier
- [Logic solver](https://php-regex.com/reference/logic-solver/): equivalence, intersection, subset, example strings
- [FAQ and Glossary](https://php-regex.com/reference/faq-glossary/): short answers and quick definitions
- [External References](https://php-regex.com/reference/resources/): the sources PHPRegex verifies diagnostics against

## Internals

- [Architecture](https://php-regex.com/architecture/): the lexer/parser/AST/visitor pipeline under the hood
- [AST traversal](https://php-regex.com/design/ast-traversal/): how the tree is walked, and in what order
- [Nodes](https://php-regex.com/nodes/): every AST node type, one per construct
- [Visitors](https://php-regex.com/visitors/): every built-in visitor, and how to build custom ones
- [Extending](https://php-regex.com/extending/): adding new PCRE features, visitors and integrations
- [Adding a lint rule](https://php-regex.com/adding-a-lint-rule/): for contributors, a lint rule from its class to its documentation and tests
- [Maintainers guide](https://php-regex.com/maintainers/): embedding PHPRegex in a tool as a first-class component
